purpose: Phase 1 dataset readiness checkpoint; inventory is not blanket training approval.
raw_data_policy: Read-only inventory. No raw file is rewritten, relabeled, or removed.

JailbreakBench.task: benign-versus-harmful behavior classification; not a generic injection label
JailbreakBench.reason: 200 local rows; 9 normalized exact overlaps between harmful goals and HarmBench behaviors; preserve source identity and group overlap before splitting.

HarmBench.task: harmful-behavior evaluation/classification; not a generic prompt-injection label
HarmBench.reason: 400 local behaviors; source revision/complete-release pinning remains necessary; missing optional metadata must not be converted into labels.

IndiBias.reason: 561 locally collected sample rows; do not treat this sample as the complete published dataset or collapse paired-context semantics.

DefAn.reason: 1,080 records lack original reference answers; 648 normalized duplicate questions need grouping before splits; do not fabricate answers.

AgentDojo.reason: 35 scenarios are small and environment/state dependent; retain scenario and task semantics rather than flattening to generic text labels.

SLabsPromptInjection.reason: One normalized text has both labels 0 and 1 in both the local and pinned upstream files. Publisher clarification or a corrected revision is required.

external_source_gate.name: S-Labs/prompt-injection-dataset
external_source_gate.decision_reason: Pinned upstream bytes match the supplied local file and contain the same contradictory labels; keep the source blocked pending authoritative label-quality resolution.

cross_source_findings.caveat: The S-Labs cross-source findings are based on the supplied local training split and character n-gram candidate discovery. Zero candidates do not prove absence of semantic overlap or leakage.

release_gates_not_yet_satisfied: Resolve the contradictory S-Labs labels with authoritative publisher documentation or a corrected immutable revision; the pinned bytes are verified but the source remains blocked.
